Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to validate Redwood on a small clinical-notes workload. Before we lock dates for a hands-on POC, the security team asked me to capture the environment steps in a MAP so we can track owners and the close timeline. Primary asks they want included: API key issuance and scoping for a temporary demo key, Redwood org setup (separate org for Acme POCs), IP allowlist entries for our egress NATs, and confirmation on VPC peering or PrivateLink options for the VPC we’d like to peer.

Can you propose a quick checklist and an estimated 2-week timeline? Also please include any artifacts we’ll need to share with our network team (CIDR/IP ranges, certificate thumbprints, contact for peering ticket).

– Sofia

Sofia — thanks, and great to hear the team is ready. I put together an initial MAP and a short onboarding checklist and attached it (poc-map-v1.xlsx). High level plan (target: 2-week POC from kickoff):

1) Week 0 (pre-kickoff, 2–3 business days):
- Redwood creates a POC organization for Acme and grants Marissa/Acme admins. (Owner: Marissa)
- Redwood issues a scoped demo API key (expires in 21 days) and documents token permissions. (Owner: Rafael)
- Acme provides the public source IPs/CIDRs to allowlist. (Owner: Sofia/IT)

2) Week 1 (kickoff + integration):
- VPC peering or PrivateLink handshake + peering ticket. Exchange of ASN/CIDR and route tables. (Owner: Acme network / Redwood SRE)
- Short smoke tests: basic generation, embeddings, and KV-cache flow. (Owner: Acme devs / Redwood SE)

3) Week 2 (load eval + close criteria):
- Run model evaluation set, measure latency and token costs. (Owner: Acme / Redwood)
- Final review and decision (accept, extend, or stop). (Owners: Sofia / Marissa)

I’ve added a checklist tab in the workbook with the exact items (API key fields, token scopes, IP ranges we need, and a preliminary VPC peering template). Rafael — can you add the technical snippets for firewall rules and the peering PR template? Ava — I’ve included you since you may need to approve the SLA exception for the demo key expiry window.

Proposed kickoff: Mon, Mar 2 — happy to move if that conflicts.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC environment onboarding and proposed MAP — technical details

Sofia / Marissa — adding the very specific network/auth snippets so Acme's ops team can copy/paste. See attached networking-snippets.txt for firewall rules and the peering checklist. Key items below:

- API key generation: We will create a scoped API key with the following scopes: generation:read, embeddings:write, sessions:manage. The key will be created in Acme's POC org and tagged "acme-demo-2026". Rafael (SE) will be the initial owner and will rotate if you want us to.

- Org setup: Provide desired org name (we suggest "Acme-POC-Redwood") and list of admin users. We will create the org and invite your admins (OIDC/SAML not required for POC).

- IP allowlist: Please allow outbound from Redwood TLS egress addresses to your endpoints if you plan to self-host callbacks. For inbound access to Redwood-hosted endpoints, add: 34.108.12.0/24, 35.190.45.0/24 (note: these are our demo egress ranges; we will confirm final ranges in vpc-reqs.pdf).

- VPC peering: We support two modes for sensitive workloads: classic VPC peering (mutual CIDR exchange + route-table updates) or PrivateLink-style (managed endpoint). Required info from Acme for peering ticket: VPC id, account id, primary CIDR, preferred route table id, and a contact. If you choose classic peering allowlist, we'll provide a step-by-step and open the peering request on our side.

- Certificates and DNS: If you need mTLS for callbacks, please provide the public cert thumbprint and the DNS name you want Redwood to contact.

I attached the small text file with iptables-friendly rules and the peering checklist. Rafael will be available for a call with your network engineer (Diego) to walk the ticket.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

Attachments: networking-snippets.txt

- Org name: "Acme-POC-Redwood" — please proceed to create.
- Admins to invite: sofia@acmehealth.com, diego.ramos@acmehealth.com, infra-team@acmehealth.com
- IPs: our NAT egress range is 52.12.32.0/24 and 52.12.33.0/24 — we can allowlist Redwood egress addresses once you confirm final list.
- Peering: Diego will run the peering ticket; we prefer PrivateLink-style endpoint if that reduces route table changes, but open to classic peering. Diego, can you sync with Rafael tomorrow at 10am PT?

One ask: for the demo we need a temporary API key scoped to the demo org and flagged "no-prod". Can you issue that before kickoff? The security team will accept a 21-day expiry for evaluation.

Sofia
